cards.text: Friend, John's Gospel opens like a song, and it starts before there was anything at all. "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God." And just so nobody misses it, John says it again: He was with God in the beginning.

cards.question: The Word was with God, and the Word was God. Through the Word, ___ things were made.

cards.text: ALL of it, baker, from every star in the sky down to every dust bunny in the back of my old junk drawer. And John says there was life in Him.

cards.question: There was life in the Word. What does John say that life was for people?

cards.text: Then John says the Light shines in the darkness. Baker, I spent YEARS in the back of a junk drawer, and one tiny crack of light had every dust bunny in there running for cover.

cards.question: John says the darkness has overcome the Light.

cards.text: Now a man shows up who was sent from God. His name was John, the one we know as John the Baptist (Matthew 3:1), and he came as a witness to testify about the Light.

cards.question: John the Baptist came to testify about the Light. Why?

answers.text: So everyone might believe through him
So people would come to follow him
So the temple leaders would listen

cards.question: John the Baptist was the Light himself.

cards.text: John the Baptist is like the sign out front of a bakery that says COOKIES. It points you right where to go, but friend, PLEASE don't try to eat the sign.
The true Light, the one who gives light to everyone, was coming into the world. He was in the world, and the world was made through Him.

cards.question: The world was made through the true Light, and now He's in it. What does the world do?

answers.text: It crowns Him as its king
It runs and hides from Him

cards.text: Picture a cookie looking up at the stamper that made it and going, "Who are YOU?" And it goes further: He came to His own, and His own did not receive Him.

cards.question: But to all who did receive the true Light and believed in His name, He gave the right to become ___ of God.
John says the children of God are born of blood or the will of man.

cards.text: They're born of God, friend. And now comes the line this whole song has been building to: "The Word became flesh and made His dwelling among us."

cards.question: John says they have seen the glory of the Word who became flesh. Whose glory is it?

answers.text: The one and only Son from the Father

cards.text: And He's full of grace and truth. Then John the Baptist cries out that the one who comes after him has surpassed him.

cards.question: John the Baptist says the one who comes after him has surpassed him because He was before him.

cards.text: Baker, when the Millers brought home a shiny new stamper, it surpassed me because it was SHARPER. This one surpasses John because He was there FIRST, and from His fullness we have all received grace upon grace.

cards.question: The law was given through Moses, Israel's leader. Grace and truth came through ___.
John says no one has ever seen God. So who has made Him known?

cards.text: The Son, who is Himself God and is at the Father's side. That's how this song ends, friend: the Word who was with God in the beginning has made Him known.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 3 quotes "Who are YOU?", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Nothing before this card introduces light. The baker can only guess the word 'light' from the line 'that life was the light of men' (John 1:4), so the pick comes down to luck and wording rather than reasoning.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to supply the wording of the line ('the light of men') instead of testing movement or meaning they can reason out.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The core action of John 1:5 is light shining in darkness without being overcome. The joke shows dust bunnies running for cover, which is a different action. Dust bunnies don't flee light, so the image doesn't click. It also clashes with his backstory, where the drawer's light was the thing he missed most.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The setup joke shows the light routing everything in the dark. That signals the answer to card 6 ('darkness has overcome the Light' is False) and rules out True before the baker answers.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card only restates John 1:8, which card 9 has just asked and answered, wrapped in a joke. It tells no new part of the passage. The joke should ride on a card that moves the passage forward.

The text says 'We have seen His glory' (John 1:14). The card says 'John says they have seen,' which changes who saw it. Coming right after the cards about the children of God, 'they' points to those children, which the text doesn't say.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The right answer is a verbatim Bible phrase ('The one and only Son from the Father') and is longer than the others. The wrong answers are plain, shorter, and awkward ('A prophet sent like Elijah'). The right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The card holds three beats: the new-stamper joke, a restatement of John 1:15 ('surpasses John because He was there FIRST'), and the new verse 16 (grace upon grace). Verse 16 is tacked onto the end of a long sentence.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: Two different people are both called 'John' with no distinction. Before John the Baptist appears, 'John' means the Gospel writer (stop 1, cards 4 and 5). After he appears, cards still say 'John says' for the writer's lines (stop 2, cards 5, 7 and 12). Stop 2 card 12 comes right after the Baptist's lines in John 1:15, so 'John says no one has ever seen God' could read as the Baptist speaking. The Gospel itself doesn't name its writer.
findings.question: How should Papa Dorin refer to the writer of John's Gospel so bakers can tell him apart from John the Baptist? For example: 'John, the Gospel writer', 'the writer', or another label. And does the 'New people' rule require saying who the writer is on the opening card?
